title: Run a table of cases
summary: test.each runs a test with each row of data. A row contains inputs and expected output.
introduction: test.each runs a test with each row of data. A row contains inputs and expected output. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain run a table of cases
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: test.each runs a test with each row of data. A row contains inputs and expected output.

blocks.code:
import { test, expect, jest, beforeEach } from "@jest/globals";
test.each([[2, 4], [3, 6], [0, 0]])("double %i is %i", (input, expected) => { expect(input * 2).toBe(expected); });

blocks.text: Jest runs three cases for the doubling rule.

blocks.text: Keep table rows small enough to understand without a second program.
